text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] p99 streaming decode latency spike (us-west1) — SLOs breached. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-20260315-42 :rotating_light:

sara: seeing a p99 jump to ~3.2s for streaming decode on prod-us-west1 around 12:03 UTC. p95 also up to 480ms. Dashboards: https://dashboards/redwood/streams?region=us-west1

devon: confirmed. Multiple service routes show tail spikes, concurrent with last nights' kernel rollout (trt8.2-rc3 + flashattn patch).

kai: adding context — we rolled trt8.2-rc3 kernel across canaries @ 02:00 UTC yesterday, then to standard pool @ 05:30 UTC. Rolling-compile flags included: `-O3 -ffast-math -fno-finite-math-only` and a new kernel compilepath change enabling `flash_attn_v2` kernels.

lena: I'm seeing increased pagefaults on hosts with nvmesh 2.1 driver. logs from one gpu host: ```
[12:02:58] pagefault: kv_cache_miss=1223 stall_us=312345
[12:03:01] decode: tail_latency_ms=3124 model=redwood-2q quant=4bit
[12:03:02] kernel: flash_attn_v2: fallback_to_generic=1
```

aj: customer-impact check: stream-heavy customers (alpha-chat, convo-express) have increased tokenization stalls and reconnects. CS ticket numbers: CS-8874, CS-8879. Mike-cs is looped.

mike-cs: confirmed at least 7 customers reported degraded streaming responsiveness; 2 customers flagged possible business impact (timeouts in web UI). We're triaging with them, can share a template message once we have mitigation plan.

sara: immediate mitigation options brainstorm: rollback kernel to trt8.1-stable on a subset; route affected requests to older model variant; enable runtime fallback for flashattn kernels (force_generic_kernels=1); throttle large-seq streams.

devon: quick check — can we route traffic by policy? `route-policy` supports region+kernel tag. We can create a temporary policy that prefers `kernel:trt8.1` for streaming routes.

kai: I can kick off a targeted rollback on 3 hosts (canary) for one cluster to validate. If that reduces p99, we can roll more. Will take ~6m per host to rebuild and verify.

lena: logs suggest the stall correlates with `kv_cache_miss` spikes and increased pagefault counts. That points to either new allocator behavior in the kernel or flashattn kernels thrashing KV memory.

ops-bot: runbook step triggered: `paging-decoder-tail` (https://runbooks/redwood/paging-decoder-tail). Ops lead: devon.

devon: taking ops lead. I'll start canary rollback now. sara — please watch SLO graphs and customer error rates. kai — do we have a safe rollback command?

kai: yes. Rollback command for kernel flavor: ```bash
./infra/deploy-tool rollback --pool streaming-us-west1 --kernel trt8.1-stable --batch 1 --wait-on-healthy
```

sara: initiating monitoring alert suppression for noisy p99 alerts to avoid alert fatigue (not silencing critical incidents).

aj: quick diagnostic metrics I pulled:
- p50 unchanged (~22ms)
- p95 moved 120ms -> 480ms
- p99 moved 650ms -> 3200ms
- streaming error-rate up 0.3% -> 1.9%
- prefix cache hit-rate dropped 89% -> 64%

lena: also grep'd kernel build metadata on one failing host: `kernel_build: trt8.2-rc3+flashv2 commit=ab12c3`

kai: rollback started on canary-01 (host id h-usw1-03). I'll post updates.

[12:09:08] kai: canary-01 rollback succeeded, restarted runtime. Initial telemetry: p99 down from 3.2s -> 1.1s (for that node's traffic).

sara: good sign. Keep stepping. devon — recommend scaling rollback batch to 3 hosts if stable for 5m.

[12:14:22] devon: rolling back 2 more hosts now (canary-02, canary-03).

aj: note — while rolling back, we should also flip `force_generic_kernels=1` in runtime config for streaming routes as a fail-safe. That toggles off flash-specific optimized kernels and avoids the KV thrash. Might increase CPU, but better than customers timing out. Risk: 10-15% p50 regression.

lena: agreed. I'm preparing the config patch: `runtime.streaming.kernel_override=generic`

[12:18:51] kai: canary-02 rollback done, canary-03 in progress. Telemetry shows aggregated p99 across cluster from 3.2s -> 1.8s after second host.

devon: rolling more now to bring affected pool down to 20% trt8.2. Monitoring for errors and memory pagefault histogram. If p99 returns near baseline, we'll hold and prepare customer comms.

ops-bot: action logged: rollback started by devon. Ticket updated: https://incidents.redwood/INC-20260315-42/updates

mike-cs: draft customer message ready, please review: "We're investigating intermittent streaming delays; mitigation in progress. We'll follow up with timeline and impact details."

sara: fine for now. Add ETA for next update at +30m.

[12:33:12] kai: full pool rollback to trt8.1 is ~60% complete for streaming-us-west1. p99 trending down to ~420ms cluster-wide. prefix cache hit-rate creeping back to ~82%.

aj: observed additional noisy errors from long-running streams that hit reconnect thresholds; suggest extending reconnect window on proxy for 1 hour.

lena: submitted runtime patch to set `force_generic_kernels=1` for streaming routes. Rolling config: `./infra/config apply --service streaming --patch "kernel_override: generic" --wait`

[12:41:00] devon: hold on further rollbacks — p99 stabilized around 420ms and streaming error-rate halved. We should keep trt8.2 out of streaming pool until further investigation.

kai: capturing forensic artifacts: heap dumps, kv-cache stats, kernel perf logs saved to s3://redwood-debug/INC-20260315-42/. Will hand off to runtime-team for root cause.

sara: next steps:
- incident severity: P1 until customer-impact resolved and p99 < 500ms for 30m.
- timeline: postmortem owner: kai; RCA deadline: 72h.
- mitigation: keep streaming pool pinned to trt8.1; disable flashattn_v2 kernels behind feature flag until QA triage.
- customer comm: mike-cs to send update in 30m.

mike-cs: will send update at 12:30 UTC.

aj: tagging impacted customers in ticket and noting that dedicated instances might be unaffected if pinned to older kernels.

[12:55:16] devon: on-call handoff to lena for next shift. Handoff notes: rollback succeeded, monitoring stable but hold P1 until RCA. See runbook steps executed in ticket.

lena: taking handoff. I'll coordinate with runtime and infra to block future trt8.2 rollout to streaming pools until signoff.

sara: thanks team. Please attach any additional logs and the `git diff` for kernel compile changes to the incident ticket.

kai: uploaded diffs and perf traces. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-20260315-42/artifacts

incident-bot: INC-20260315-42 status: mitigated -> monitoring. P1 remains open for RCA.

mike-cs: customer update posted: "Mitigation deployed — traffic rerouted and kernel rollback in progress. We're monitoring; next update in 30 minutes." :white_check_mark: 

sara: closing convo here; move follow-ups to the incident ticket and rca doc. Great run. :thumbsup:
